To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

supplemental irrigation applied at the reproductive stage and sowing in the first two weeks of April, rather than in May or June, maximizes grain yield of mid-flowering fababean cultivars in south-eastern Australian conditions.
supplemental irrigation during the vegetative stage and late sowing date increased grain yield, water use efficiency, harvest index, and seed weight.

the highest grain yield was obtained from the reproductive-stage irrigated SD1 (5.85 t ha−1) while the highest water productivity was obtained from the SD1-fully (1.65  kg m-3) and SD2-reproductively (1.63  kg m- 3) irrigated treatments.

the development of a management strategy for faba bean that minimizes the year to year variability in grain yield.

the best irrigation strategy for faba bean production is to irrigate from the mid-September to end October and to sow in the first week in April.

the mid-flowering cultivar can be grown under semiarid conditions with a supplemental irrigation applied from the mid-September to October.
